A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 35-page versions of the same VTI/CoSMIC research. Text and visual inspection support comparison of the main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G despite the title change.

before.justification: v2 reports original robust variable selection experiments, nonlinear DAG simulations, and inference results on Sachs flow cytometry data in Section 5 and Appendices F–G.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their outcomes, including the numerical comparison in Table 1 and results in Figures 2–11.

M1.justification: Sections 2–3 retain the same CoSMIC masking and permutation construction, variational objective, model distributions, and optimization procedures. Replacing 'amortized' with 'flow-based' does not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same robust variable selection scenarios, 10-node DAG simulations, and 11-node flow cytometry data. The application examples added to the abstract and the expanded Section 5.2 heading introduce no new coverage.

E2.justification: RJMCMC remains the variable selection reference. Figure 4 retains DAGMA, DiBS, DiBS+, and JSP-GFN; Table 1 retains DAGMA, DiBS+, and JSP-GFN. The compared variational families and model samplers are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Data generation, cardinality and sample-size sweeps, training budgets, model configurations, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices A, F, and G, including Figure 3's 30,000-iteration budget.

E4.justification: Both retain the same flow-expressivity and cardinality studies, misspecification and prior-width analyses, and posterior visual comparisons in Figures 2–3 and 5–11 and Appendix F.

E5.justification: Figure 4 still reports means and standard errors over nine repetitions. Appendix G.3 still describes ten VTI seed replicates and selection by minimum terminal loss. Repeated-run disclosures and uncertainty reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 and Figures 2–11 retain the same results. For example, VTI's Table 1 scores remain F1 0.44, SHD 23.0, Brier 23.0, and AUROC 0.68; DiBS+ retains its lower Brier score of 17.0.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, and proofs in Sections 2–3 and Appendices B–E are unchanged, including CoSMIC density factorization and the GP-surrogate convergence guarantee.

C1.justification: Both claim a single CoSMIC variational density for transdimensional inference, joint VTI training, and scalability to large model spaces. Removing 'amortized' and naming existing applications changes the framing without changing the substantive contributions or their scope.

C2.justification: The discussion retains the same explanations of approximation quality, suppression of poorly approximated models, mode collapse, and future work. Appendix F's interpretation of prior sensitivity and posterior comparisons is also unchanged.

D1.justification: The code-availability footnote, CoSMIC implementation details, data-generation instructions, baseline settings, and RTX3090/H100 hardware and precision disclosures remain unchanged in page 2 and Appendices A, F, and G.

R1.justification: Dayan et al.'s The Helmholtz Machine is removed and Hoffman et al.'s Stochastic Variational Inference is added. The opening now cites stochastic optimization, including the already-listed Paisley et al. work. Section 4's substantive comparisons remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The title becomes Variational Transdimensional Inference. Localized edits replace 'amortized' terminology, add abstract application examples, expand the Section 5.2 heading, and acknowledge Daniel M. Steinberg. Section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3's caption replaces 'amortized' with 'flow-based', and introductory text and references reflow across page boundaries. The graphics, table structures, and placement of experimental displays otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 makes limited terminology and background-citation refinements, particularly in the title and opening description of variational inference. The substantive argument, proofs, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information remain equivalent across the main text and appendices. These small editorial changes do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
